Subject: Dedicated capacity perf validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Samantha / Kevin,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLOs and the Dedicated capacity validation plan.

Key SLOs you shared:
- 95th percentile latency target: 100–150 ms for single-turn text generation (avg input ~256 tokens)
- Sustained throughput: ~600 tokens/sec (aggregate across service)
- Concurrency: target steady-state of 30 concurrent requests with burst to 60 for short periods
- Streaming: yes — token-level streaming required to the client with <50 ms per-chunk delivery

What we need from your side to size a Dedicated pool and run a validation:
1) Representative prompt set (a sample of inputs or a short dataset) — helps with sequence length distribution
2) Expected ratio of short chat vs long generation (approx % of requests >512 tokens)
3) Any hard limits on single-request latency or p50/p95 targets for specific endpoints

Next steps (Redwood):
- Rafael to propose GPU family comparisons (A100 vs H100/80GB vs L4-like inference options) and initial reserved throughput sizing (this week)
- We'll deliver a perf test plan and propose canary run dates (attached: perf_test_plan.xlsx)
- Post canary, share detailed cost/latency tradeoffs and recommended commit sizes

If the above looks right, I’ll loop in Neha for billing/contract prelims and set up the test window.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity perf validation — GPU comparisons & test plan

Hi Samantha / Kevin,

Following up with the technical breakdown and proposed validation approach. High-level summary first, then test plan.

GPU family comparison (expected behavior for your workload):
- A100 40GB (mixed precision inference): good baseline for general transformer workloads; expected p95 in our tests ~130–180ms at 30 concurrent for the model family you described; scales reasonably but memory limits make long sequences more expensive.
- H100 80GB: best p95 and headroom for concurrency; we typically see p95 ~90–140ms at 30–60 concurrency and better headroom for spikes. Higher cost but lower latency and better multi-model density.
- L4-like inference GPUs (cost-optimized): good for cost-sensitive usage with quantized models; p95 will be higher (often 180–300ms) but unit cost significantly lower. Streaming behavior depends on kernel optimizations — we recommend careful quantization profiles.

Recommended reserved sizing for your SLOs (initial proposal):
- Start with a 3-node pool of H100-80GB (reserved) to meet 95th <150ms with room for bursts. We estimate sustained throughput ~700–900 tokens/sec depending on batching/kv-cache.
- Alternatively, a hybrid pool: 2x H100 + 2x A100 to balance cost and headroom; route steady traffic to A100s and reserve H100s for spikes and heavy long-seq requests.

Proposed validation plan (attached plan and small canary):
1) Canary run (2 hours) on a representative subset — focus on p50/p95, streaming chunk latency, and per-node concurrency.
2) Full load run (4 hours) simulating steady-state + burst windows to validate autoscaling and reserved throughput.
3) Collect per-token latency distribution, kernel-level metrics, GPU utilization, and memory headroom.
4) Produce a short report with cost estimates and recommended commit size.

Attachments included: gpu_compare-20270218.pdf (detailed numbers), perf_test_plan.xlsx (test schedule/tasks). I’ll run a quick canary on Feb 23 morning if that works for your team.

Notes on streaming: our runtime supports sub-50ms chunk delivery on H100 for most token sizes, but client-side buffering and network hops can add 20–40ms. We’ll instrument end-to-end to isolate where any additional latency occurs.

Let me know whether Feb 23 AM works; if so, I’ll book infra and share the canary run checklist.

Thanks,
Rafael
